why: Every anchor, attribute and rule of isAppAddress() is named, and unit tests hold the pay-path boundary. The risk is what a soft navigation changes that the checks only partly see: tracking tools started by the consent banner, A/B click goals counted by data-block-id, entrance motion and owners' custom CSS all ran on a fresh document before. The brief lists the e2e specs that should catch it, but a wrong pass-through (a lost data-* attribute in one branch, or plain not threaded to an inner function of page-block.tsx so the builder canvas prefetches) could still pass. The change also sits on the PCI rule that every entry into a pay route is a full page load.
harm_if_wrong: A block that drops data-block-id or data-hover in the PolicyLink branch would quietly stop A/B goals counting or hover effects on every built page, and a mistake in isAppAddress() would let a press move into checkout without the full page load PCI's CSP rule relies on.
make_it_cheaper: Add to block-link.test.ts a case that renders BlockLink with every listed attribute (data-block-id, data-hover, data-button-frame, data-kz-text, style, aria-*) in both branches and compares the two outputs apart from data-policy, so a dropped attribute fails without e2e.
brief_problems: The e2e target is written 'e2e/{prefetch.spec.ts}' and said to be made by step 1.3; step 1.3's brief says step 0.12 creates it and 1.3 extends it.
Depends on step 2.6's src/components/policy-link.tsx with an 'intent' policy, which does not exist today (stop_if covers it).
